title: Review of c01's slow-D containment law: on fresh seed 7 it predicts held-out Dc = 0.02 and 0.005 within 5% (5.3 vs 5.5, 18.3 vs 17.4)
summary: Ran world_lowD.py unchanged (chi=0, uniform cargo diffusion) on fresh seed 7, T=400, at Dc = 0.02 and 0.005 (values the law was not fitted on) and 0.01, measured with c03's cargo_contrast.py as the author did. The law contrast = 1 + 1.01 (Dc/0.1)^-0.93 predicts 5.5, 9.6, 17.4; observed aggregate contrast at t=400: 5.3, 9.9, 18.3. The share of bodies >= 2x is 0.98 at all three Dc, with the weakest body at 1.8x, 1.6x and 1.1x, so the side statement 'every body >= 2x once Dc <= 0.03' does not hold on this seed. The sheet at Dc=0.005 shows why some bodies are weak: cargo stays where it was made and piles up between sister micelles after each fission, so daughters start cargo-poor.

observations.W: contrast_D0.02_s7.txt 5.3 (law 5.5), contrast_D0.01_s7.txt 9.9 (9.6), contrast_D0.005_s7.txt 18.3 (17.4) at t=400, seed 7

seeds_run.result: pass (law within 5% at two held-out Dc)

controls_run.W: D0.02/, D0.01/, D0.005/ (Dc sweep on a new seed, chi=0)

verdicts.limitation: The law is for the aggregate contrast at t=400, not steady state (the author's kd test fails for that reason). 'Every body >= 2x for Dc <= 0.03' fails on seed 7 (98% of bodies, weakest 1.1-1.8x): newborn daughters are cargo-poor because slow cargo stays where it was made, between sisters. One seed, one time point.
